Highway Department
The Highway Department maintains close to 302 highway miles and 109 bridges in Tompkins County. The mission of the Highway Department is to provide highway and bridge construction, maintenance, and emergency services safely, effectively, and efficiently for our local and traveling public customers, while promoting self-esteem and growth as individuals.
Road Maintenance staff construct, maintain, and repair roads, maintain intersections and roadside drainage, eliminate roadside hazards, and repair guiderails. The Tompkins County Highway Department also maintains more than 5,000 signs.
Weights and Measures

Ever wonder who maintains the road in front of your property?
Mapping Tompkins has an interactive tool that allows you to click on any road within the County to see who is responsible for maintaining it:
Road Maintenance Mapper
Hint: If using the search bar, only put in the road name (example: "Bostwick Rd") or scrolling in on the map and searching for the property and then double clicking on the roadway to see who maintains that section.

Tompkins County Highway Department
Department Head
Nicholas Ensign
Nicholas (Nick) Ensign joined the Tompkins County Highway Department in July 2018. He was initially hired as a Senior Crew Supervisor, later promoted to Deputy Director, and ultimately appointed Director of Highway in August 2025.
His collaborative approach has helped foster a regional network focused on sharing best practices and developing innovative solutions that strengthen County operations.
